title: QDG-Like Matter in the Lauscher–Reuter R2 Truncation: Branch Structure, Regulator Dependence and Comparison with the Einstein–Hilbert Flow
content: We compute the minimally coupled scalar, Dirac, Maxwell and Proca contributions to the three projections of the Lauscher--Reuter (LR) \( R^2 \) truncation on \( S^4 \), and validate the heat-kernel coefficients against exact spectral sums. In LR's single-coupling \( S^4 \) projection the matter contribution assigned to \( R^2 \) is \( Z=\sum_i(\varrho_i-a_i/6) \); this clarifies the projection convention discussed in the companion preprint rather than correcting a projection-independent coefficient. Along the QDG-like line (two massless-limit Proca fields and \( n_f \) Dirac fermions), the branch connected to the LR pure-gravity fixed point has three relevant directions at \( n_f=3 \) for the original five exponential regulators \( s\in[1,2] \), but this conclusion is fragile: the expanded exponential scan includes \( s=0.5 \), where B1 is not admissible at \( n_f=3 \), and the Litim continuation connected to pure gravity reaches an \( \eta_N \) pole near \( n_f\simeq1.7 \). A second branch exists at \( n_f=3 \) for the original five-regulator scan, but lies very close to the \( \eta_N \) pole and is more fragile; it is not equivalent to B1 and its large-\( n_f \) continuation is outside the conventional range \( g_*<2 \), \( \lambda_*>-1 \). An exploratory scan of a structurally distinct smooth family \( R^{(0)}(y)=e^{-y^n} \) (\( n=2,3 \)) finds an admissible branch-connected point at \( n_f=3 \) for \( n=3 \), while the \( n=2 \) point lies in the low-accuracy near-pole region; this two-shape check is not a robustness proof. The Einstein--Hilbert comparison shows that regulator and gravitational-scheme effects both contribute to differences from the companion preprint; \( g_* \) and \( \lambda_* \) are not universal. The Weyl-gauged sector of QDG is not included, so these results do not establish asymptotic safety of QDG.
